conviction_note: Findings sum to +0.6 (a known $60.4M GAAP gain and ~7% GAAP book-value lift from the Albertsons sale, loan-book growth, activist optionality and a washed-out sector, against a 17.5% yield that prices a dividend cut). The scaled number is slightly negative: abs_move 5.0 x (2*0.48-1). The last two prints were sold (-4.58, -4.45), the bar is disputed ($0.11 vs $0.14) and the dividend question can swing it either way. The gap in sign comes from the reaction function: this name has sold its last two prints, and the positives are mostly one-off or already disclosed.
bar: Disputed. Q3 2026 adjusted distributable EPS consensus $0.11 per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BRSP/earnings-forecasts) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BRSP), but $0.14 (7 analysts, range $0.13-0.15) per Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BRSP/analysis/). Q2 actual ADE was $0.13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001717547/000171754726000059/brspq226earningsrelease0.htm). There is no company guide, so every size on the name is capped small. print_vs_bar is read against a ~$0.13 midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest is low: about 5.5M shares, 1.96 days to cover at the 2026-06-30 settlement, and about 2.9% of float per an undated Equibles snapshot (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/BRSP/short-interest/, https://equibles.com/stocks/BRSP). Not a crowded short. No usable option chain (16 contracts of open interest, put/call OI 0.33), so there is no skew. The stock is -30% since the Q2 print (5.24 to 3.665, Yahoo chart), at 2% above its 52-week low, ~0.54x Q2 GAAP book of $6.81 and ~0.45x undepreciated book of $8.10, with a 17.5% yield on the $0.16 dividend. The whole commercial mREIT group fell with it from Jul 28 to Oct 27 (Yahoo spark): BXMT -37%, TRTX -26%, STWD -25%, ACRE -25%, FBRT -18%, KREF -18%. Activist Cottonwood (CW Investment Advisers) holds 8.7% at an average cost of ~$5.68.

findings.finding: The Albertsons Net Lease 1 sale closed 2026-09-14 for $300.0M ($97.9M net cash plus $200M of debt assumed). The 8-K pro forma shows a gain on sale of $60.4M, about $0.48 per share on ~126.8M shares, and a GAAP equity lift from $862.98M to $923.38M, roughly +$0.47 per share on Q2's $6.81 book value. Q3 GAAP EPS and GAAP book value will therefore print far above the $0.11-0.14 ADE consensus and Q2's -$0.15 GAAP loss, before any Q3 reserve moves.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior quarter carried a gain of this size. Q2 2024 had a large GAAP loss (-$0.53) from office equity alongside a dividend cut. The baseline shows the last two prints at -4.58 and -4.45 on ADE and credit, not on GAAP.
findings.why_not_priced: The pro forma is public, but consensus feeds carry ADE, which excludes realized gains, so the headline GAAP EPS and book value will screen as a large beat and a book increase. If the market had priced a ~7% GAAP book increase, the stock would not have fallen 17% since the 9/16 filing to 0.54x pre-gain book. Economically, much of the gain is depreciation recapture, so undepreciated book (the $8.10 figure management and the activist quote) moves much less. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The sale terms and Q3 closing are corroborated by the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-brightspire-capital-inc-stock/) and the 8-K item 2.01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1717547/000171754726000065/brsp-20260914.htm). Both rest on the same transaction.

findings.finding: The loan book grew into Q3: just over $3B in late July (from $2.9B at the Q2 release), with $117M closed after quarter end, $178M in execution, and July originations nearly equal to all of Q2. BRSP then closed the $960M BRSP 2026-FL4 CRE CLO on 2026-10-16 (A notes at SOFR+1.40%) and redeemed the 2024-FL2 CLO with cash on hand. Higher average earning assets support Q3 ADE at or above Q2's $0.13, which beats the $0.11 Benzinga/EW bar and is in line with Yahoo's $0.14. Partial offset: lost Albertsons NOI of ~$10M per half-year, net of 4.77% interest on $200M, for the last ~2 weeks of the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed $0.13 ADE (a beat on Benzinga, a miss vs Yahoo's $0.15) and the stock went -4.58. Q1 2026 printed $0.14 against higher estimates and the stock went -4.45. This name has not paid for in-line ADE.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar itself is split ($0.11 vs $0.14), so part of the street is modelling a decline that loan growth argues against. If growth were priced, the stock would not trade at a 17.5% yield. Capped small because the bar is disputed and the name sold its last two ADE prints.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on post-quarter closings and the $3.5B year-end target (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-brightspire-capital-inc-stock/). That is a different document from the CLO 8-K.

findings.finding: Dividend coverage is the open question. Q2 ADE was $0.13 against the $0.16 dividend (81%). Management said the Albertsons sale delays full coverage by about two quarters, to Q2/Q3 2027. At $3.665 the $0.16 quarterly payout yields 17.5%, which prices a cut. The Q3 dividend was already declared on 2026-09-14 and the Q4 one is normally declared mid-December (prior declarations June 15 and Sept 14), so a formal cut is unlikely in this release. But BRSP did announce its 2024 cut ($0.20 to $0.16) inside a Q2 earnings release, and call commentary on the Q4 dividend can move the stock either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2024-07-30 release carried the cut to $0.16 alongside a -$0.53 GAAP loss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1717547/000171754724000068/brspq224earningsreleasev.htm). The baseline does not isolate that day's move.
findings.why_not_priced: The yield shows a cut is largely priced. Formally reaffirming $0.16 would be a positive surprise, and a cut announced early would still be a negative event: after the 2024 cut the stock carried a lower yield. Sized slightly negative because a lowered payout target is the more likely content, and the reaction to an affirmation is capped by the coverage arithmetic.
findings.independence: Q3 $0.16 declaration on 2026-09-14 (https://finviz.com/news/391802/brightspire-capital-announces-016-per-share-dividend-for-third-quarter-2026). Q2 2024 cut precedent from a different document (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240730915214/en/brightspire-capital-inc.-announces-second-quarter-2024-financial-results).

findings.finding: Activist and capital return: Cottonwood/CW Investment Advisers (Hon Kit Shing) owns 10.98M shares (8.7%) at an average cost of ~$5.68. Its funds added in Sept at $4.49-4.65. It converted to a 13D on 2026-09-29 after the board twice (Aug 12, Sept 14) refused to waive the 9.8% ownership limit, and it lists a sale, merger, board changes and capitalization proposals as possible actions. BRSP had $29M left on its buyback after buying 3.8M shares at $5.46 in Q2, and received $97.9M of cash from the Albertsons sale. The release and 10-Q cover will show Q3 buyback activity and share count, and the call is the first public venue to answer the 13D.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior activist episode at BRSP. The Q2 'largest buyback in history' quarter still traded -4.58.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell from 4.03 to 3.665 after the 13D was filed, so the market assigns the activist little value. A buyback at ~$4 against $8.10 undepreciated book, or a board response (strategic review, waiver), would be news. Most likely nothing is said, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Exhibit 1 transactions in the same filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1717547/000092189526002666/ex1sc13d14949001_09292026.htm), the same document. Buyback figures from the Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-28-brightspire-capital-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: Financing: on or before 2026-10-19 BRSP redeemed the 2024-FL2 CLO in full with cash on hand, alongside the new $960M FL4 CLO. The money buys a refinanced, larger, match-funded loan book with a 30-month reinvestment period, which corroborates the stated ramp to $3.5B. It also uses cash that could have gone to buybacks, and likely brings an accelerated deferred-financing write-off, a GAAP Q4 item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FL3 CLO closed in Feb 2026 (redeeming FL1) and that print went +0.52.
findings.why_not_priced: The filing is public. Its value is in what management says about the funding cost and capacity on the call. It is a financing item that funds visible originations, so it is signed small positive.
findings.independence: Shares the 8-K with the loan-growth finding, so the two together count once on the CLO fact. That finding rests on the Q2 call, this one on the financing structure.

findings.finding: Sector positioning: the commercial mREIT peer group fell hard from 2026-07-28 to 2026-10-27 (BXMT -37%, TRTX -26%, STWD -25%, ACRE -25%, FBRT -18%, KREF -18%) and BRSP -30%. When the group bounced on 2026-10-22 (TRTX +6.3%, BXMT +3.7%, STWD +3.7%), BRSP rose only +0.8%. The bar for credit commentary is low, but this is a proxy and the name has sold its last two prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints went -4.58 and -4.45, both into falling sector tapes. The baseline shows 3 of 7 prints up.
findings.why_not_priced: It is price data, so by definition it is in the price. The only claim is asymmetry: at 0.45x undepreciated book, a quiet credit quarter has more room up than down. It is a proxy, so it carries little weight. The same sector fall also implies peers are seeing credit stress (KREF strategic review, BXMT office defaults), which could show up as more CECL at BRSP.
findings.independence: KREF strategic review (https://www.credaily.com/briefs/kkr-real-estate-finance-trust-weighs-sale-or-merger-options/?.tsrc=rss) supports the sector-stress reading. No company-level confirmation.

findings.finding: Watch-list and REO items guided for Q3: Mesa AZ multifamily REO sale expected to close in Q3, two multifamily REOs under contract (NAV $62M), the $11M Denver office watch-list loan expected to be sold near term, Austin multifamily and Dallas office loans possibly resolved, the Aurora office net-lease debt maturing in August with an extension under negotiation, and a $57M Las Vegas multifamily loan added to the watch list in Q2. General CECL was already raised to $100M (327 bps).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 resolved three risk-rank-5 loans with a $1M charge-off and the stock went -4.58 on the print.
findings.why_not_priced: These items are inside what management guided, so they are expected. Only a surprise (Aurora default, new risk-rank 5s) would move the stock, and nothing public points to one. Sized at zero, with a range skewed down.

outside_window.finding: Q4 dividend declaration, normally mid-December (Q2 declared June 15, Q3 Sept 14). The formal cut-or-hold decision most likely lands then.
Cottonwood 13D escalation: possible proposals on board composition or a sale, with timing undated.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to cut against. The -9% 20-day and -30% since-print drawdown, a sector move, leaves a low bar, which my small net-positive findings agree with. The name's own reaction function (the last two prints sold about 4.5%) cuts against them, so p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): the $60.4M Albertsons GAAP gain resized from +0.8 to +0.5, a fraction of the same dollars as operating profit, because most of it is depreciation recapture with no path to ADE or the guide.
Lesson 6 (disputed bar, $0.11 vs $0.14): the loan-growth ADE finding capped from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lessons 1 and 5 (this name sold its last two prints; the sector move is a proxy): the sector-positioning finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (about 2 days to cover, not crowded), so the dividend negative was left at -0.8.
Left standing: the dividend, activist, financing and watch-list findings, abs_move_pct 5.0 and p_up 48.
